title: SEA-FGT: Frequency-Guided Transformer with Semantic Expert Augment for Time Series Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Practical multivariate time-series anomaly detection is difficult because real-world data contain complex inter-channel dependencies and subtle anomaly-induced perturbations.

gap.claim: Empirically designed augmentations struggle to increase pattern diversity while preserving semantic consistency because time series have implicit semantics and heterogeneity.

contributions.claim: SEA-FGT combines frequency-aware modeling for cross-channel dependencies and spectral perturbations with semantic expert augmentation that adaptively aligns augmentations with diverse temporal semantics.
The paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of semantic expert augmentation, extending diversity criteria to conditional formulations and proving a representation-robustness bound.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on multiple real-world datasets report competitive performance against state-of-the-art baselines across diverse evaluation metrics.
Additional explorations and visualizations are reported to corroborate the method's effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multivariate time-series anomaly detection is important for industrial monitoring and intelligent operations.
Deployment is difficult because of complex dependencies and subtle anomaly perturbations.
Existing empirical augmentations face difficulty balancing pattern diversity with semantic consistency.
SEA-FGT addresses these challenges through frequency-aware modeling and semantic expert augmentation.
The paper reports theoretical analysis and competitive empirical results with supporting explorations and visualizations.

source_observation.claim: The method combines frequency-domain modeling with augmentation conditioned on temporal semantics.

interpretation.claim: Modeling signal structure and augmentation semantics jointly may help address both dependency complexity and semantic inconsistency.

application.claim: For multivariate temporal anomaly detection, consider frequency-aware representations together with semantics-aware augmentation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination is beneficial outside the reported datasets, metrics, and deployment conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, baseline methods, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, training procedure, computational cost, or implementation details.
The abstract does not specify the assumptions or scope of the theoretical robustness bound.
